inspection_comments: No violations observed at time of inspection. Gloves were available for preventing bare hand contact with ready to eat food items such as sliced tomatoes and lettuce when preparing salads. A working digital probe thermometer was available to ensure that potentially hazardous food items (PHF) such as raw chicken wings are cooked to 165F or above. Observed required cold holding temperatures (45F or below) of PHF in drawer refrigeration unit under flat top grill such as raw bacon (actual 38F). Facility was adequately logging discard times to use time as a public health control instead of temperature for holding PHF such as calzones with cooked veggie toppings in the counter top display case. Facility was adequately cooling PHF such as cooked penne noodles in the walk-in cooler in shallow (less than 4 inches) uncovered containers in the walk-in cooler. Discussed that PHF is to be cooled from 120F to 70F within 2 hours and from 70F-45F within an additional 4 hours for a total cooling schedule of 6 hours. No PHF were being hot held in facility at time of inspection. Discussed that required hot holding temperatures of PHF is 140F or above. Test strips were available to ensure that chlorine sanitizing solution is at a strength of at least 50ppm for sanitizing dishes/utensils and at least 100ppm for sanitizing food contact surfaces.

inspection_comments: No violations observed during inspection. Gloves and tongs were available to prevent bare hand contact with ready to eat food items such as popcorn. Facility additionally cools PHF such as red sauce with ice wands and cools cooked noodles with an ice bath. A working digital probe thermometer was available to ensure that PHF such as meatballs made with raw ground beef are cooked to 158F or above. Test strips were available to ensure that chlorine sanitizing solution is at a strength of at least 50ppm for sanitizing dishes/utensils and at least 100ppm for sanitizing food contact surfaces.
